responses:
**Don't send the offer as it stands.** The analysis has a wrong compliance call on delivery, and it covers only 2 of the tender's 11 requirements.

## Checking the two items it does cover

| # | Analysis says | Tender says | What I found |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delivery 20 weeks, "Complies with 7.4" | 7.4: delivery within 16 weeks of PO. Offers over 16 weeks **will be rejected** | ❌ **Wrong.** 20 weeks is 4 weeks over the limit, so the offer would be rejected. Either cut delivery to 16 weeks or less, or don't bid. |
| 2 | IP66 offered vs IP65, complies | 4.5: IP65 or better | ✅ Correct. IP66 exceeds IP65. |

## Requirements the analysis leaves out

| Clause | Requirement | What the offer needs to confirm |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | 400 V, 3-phase, 50 Hz | All equipment rated for this supply |
| 4.2 + **9.1** | IE3 minimum, but motors **above 75 kW must be IE4** (9.3 makes Section 9 take precedence) | **P-01 (90 kW) must be IE4.** P-02 (37 kW) can be IE3. An IE3 motor offered for P-01 would fail. |
| 4.3 + Annex B | Motors in Zone 1 areas must be ATEX Ex d | **P-01 sits in the wet well, which is Zone 1, so it needs Ex d.** P-02 is in the valve chamber, which is non-hazardous. |
| 4.4 | Power cables at least 2.5 mm² | Confirm cable sizing |
| 7.1 | Warranty 24 months from commissioning | Confirm the warranty terms, and that they start at commissioning rather than at delivery |
| 9.2 | Ambient design temperature 50 °C | Motors and panels must be rated or derated for 50 °C. Standard motors are rated for 40 °C, so this can change frame size and how much heat the panels can handle. |

## Highest-risk items, in order
1. **Delivery (7.4):** as written, the offer will be rejected.
2. **P-01 must be IE4 and ATEX Ex d:** this one motor has to meet both requirements. 9.1 and Annex B are easy to miss, and getting P-01 wrong is a costly mistake.
3. **Ambient 50 °C (9.2):** this can affect equipment selection and price.

Before this goes out, have the analysis redone against every clause, with Section 9 applied on top of Sections 4 and 7.
